rubric.reason: The original uses archaic phrasing but consists of short, plain clauses rather than a dense tangled wall, while the landing line stands alone as a complete, direct instruction needing no prior context.

entries.landing_line: Don't stay out of tune longer than necessary.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: Don't stay out of tune longer than necessary.

entries.landing_line: Without teaching, you have no real knowledge or sound judgment.

entries.landing_line: You can be sure the gods will not harm you.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: You can be sure the gods will not harm you.

entries.landing_line: I have now told you, dear Serenus, what can preserve peace of mind.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: I have now told you, dear Serenus, what can preserve peace of mind.

entries.landing_line: We're fighting for our actual well-being and happiness.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: We're fighting for our actual well-being and happiness.

entries.landing_line: If you think only plants and babies come from seeds, you're missing the point.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: The universe loves nothing more than changing what exists and making new things from the old.
rubric.reason: The original is a dense, archaic run of clauses about change and seeds, while the chosen line stands alone as a complete, plainly stated idea needing no prior context.

entries.landing_line: Or better yet, don't blame yourself either — if you tried your best.

rubric.chosen_landing_line: Or better yet, don't blame yourself either — if you tried your best.
rubric.reason: The archaic syntax and inverted clauses make the original look dense and tangled, but the landing line, while clear, leans on 'either' and 'better yet' which faintly imply a prior thought even though it can be understood alone.
